mainTopic: יוצא דופן (caesarean birth): the מחלוקת between the רבנן and רבי שמעון about the laws of a יולדת, the פסוקים each side uses, and רבי יוחנן's rule that a יוצא דופן animal cannot become קדשים
overview: The משנה teaches three rules. First, the רבנן say a caesarean birth (יוצא דופן) does not give the mother the days of טומאה and טהרה or the קרבן of a יולדת, while רבי שמעון says it counts like a normal birth. Second, a woman becomes טמאה once blood reaches the בית החיצון, but a זב and a בעל קרי become טמא only when the discharge leaves the body, in any amount. The גמרא then traces each side's sources. The רבנן use ״תזריע״ to exclude a caesarean birth and ״תלד״ to include a טומטום and an אנדרוגינוס. רבי שמעון uses ״תלד״ for a caesarean birth and ״לבן או לבת״ for the טומטום. The two sides also differ on which words teach that separate births need separate קרבנות: ״זאת״ for רבי שמעון, ״לבן או לבת״ for the רבנן. רבי יוחנן adds that even רבי שמעון agrees an animal born by caesarean cannot become קדשים, learning it from בכור rather than אדם because בכור shares more features with קדשים. Finally, a ברייתא of רבי יהודה is brought to support רבי יוחנן, and it continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A caesarean birth and the laws of a יולדת
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that for a baby born by caesarean section, the mother does not keep the days of טומאה and טהרה and brings no קרבן. רבי שמעון disagrees and says it counts like a normal birth.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: For a baby born by caesarean section, the mother does not keep the days of impurity and the days of purity, and she does not have to bring an offering. רבי שמעון says: this baby is like one born normally.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה opens with a מחלוקת: does a caesarean birth (יוצא דופן) give the mother the special laws of a woman who gave birth?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a יולדת is טמאה for 7 or 14 days, then has 33 or 66 days of טהרה, and afterward brings a קרבן. The unnamed first opinion (the רבנן) says none of this applies to a caesarean birth. רבי שמעון says it is treated exactly like a regular birth.

keyTerms.meaning: A baby born through the wall of the abdomen (caesarean section)
The days of impurity after birth (7 for a boy, 14 for a girl)
The days of purity after birth (33 for a boy, 66 for a girl)
The offering a woman brings after childbirth
Like a baby born in the normal way

steps.confusionAlert: The question here is only about the mother's laws as a יולדת. The baby is fully a baby either way. The מחלוקת is about whether this kind of birth brings the יולדת laws for the mother.

phrases.english: MISHNAH: One born by caesarean section —
phrases.notes: Literally "one who comes out through the wall," meaning through the wall of the mother's belly.

phrases.english: they do not observe for it
days of impurity and days of purity,
and they are not obligated to bring an offering for it.
Rabbi Shimon says:
This is like one who was born normally.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opening of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the רבנן, a caesarean birth does not bring the days of טומאה and טהרה or the קרבן. According to רבי שמעון, it is treated like a normal birth.

steps.title: Women become impure from blood inside, men only once it comes out
steps.stepSummary: A woman becomes טמאה once blood reaches the בית החיצון, even before it leaves her body. A זב or בעל קרי becomes טמא only when the discharge actually comes out.
steps.simpleTranslation: All women become impure when blood reaches the outer chamber, as it says: "Her discharge in her flesh shall be blood." But a זב and one who had a seminal emission do not become impure until their impurity comes out of the body.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a new rule about the point at which a person becomes טמא from a bodily discharge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a woman, the פסוק says "בבשרה", "in her flesh," so blood still inside her body (in the בית החיצון) already makes her טמאה. For a זב and a בעל קרי there is no such word, so they become טמא only when the discharge leaves the body.

keyTerms.meaning: The outer chamber, an inner part of the woman's body outside the womb
Her discharge in her flesh, which shows impurity even while the blood is still inside
A man with a gonorrhea-like discharge that makes him impure
A man who had a seminal emission

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the next case: since a man becomes טמא only when the emission leaves his body, he can stop it from coming out in time.

phrases.english: All women become impure
in the outer chamber,
as it is stated: "Her discharge in her flesh shall be blood,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 15:19

phrases.english: but the zav and one who had a seminal emission
do not become impure
until their impurity comes outside.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new, separate rule in the same משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Women become טמאה once blood reaches the בית החיצון. A זב and a בעל קרי become טמא only when the discharge leaves the body.

steps.title: The כהן eating תרומה who feels an emission coming
steps.stepSummary: A כהן eating תרומה who feels an emission coming may hold it in and swallow the תרומה while still טהור. The משנה adds that these discharges make a person טמא in any amount, even smaller than a mustard seed.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a כהן was eating תרומה and felt his limbs tremble, he holds his organ and swallows the תרומה. And these discharges make a person impure in any amount, even as small as a mustard seed, and even less than that.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה applies the rule just taught to a practical case and then adds that there is no minimum size for this טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since a man becomes טמא only once the emission leaves his body, the כהן can hold it in and finish swallowing while he is still טהור. The last line teaches that once it does come out, even the tiniest amount makes him טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: The holy portion of produce given to a כהן, which he may eat only while pure
His limbs trembled, a sign that an emission is about to happen
In any amount at all
Mustard seed, a classic example of something tiny

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה has three parts: יוצא דופן is a מחלוקת between the רבנן and רבי שמעון; a woman is טמאה from blood inside, while men are טמא only when the discharge comes out; and a man's discharge makes him טמא in any amount.

phrases.english: If he was eating teruma,
and he felt that his limbs trembled —
he holds his organ
and swallows the teruma,
And they make impure in any amount,
even like a mustard seed,
and even less than that.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the rule from step 2 to a practical case and adds that there is no minimum amount
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כהן may hold back an emission and finish eating תרומה while טהור. The discharge of a זב and a בעל קרי makes a person טמא in any amount.

steps.title: What is the reason of the רבנן about caesarean birth?
steps.stepSummary: רבי מני בר פטיש asks for the source of the רבנן's view that a caesarean birth does not bring the laws of a יולדת.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רבי מני בר פטיש said: What is the reason of the רבנן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the first part of the משנה and asks where the רבנן get their rule. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is about the רבנן specifically, the first opinion in step 1, who say יוצא דופן does not count as a birth. A source is needed, because a baby was clearly born.

keyTerms.meaning: What is their reason?
The Sages, here the unnamed first opinion in the משנה

phrases.aramaic: גְּמָ' אָמַר רַבִּי מָנִי בַּר פַּטִּישׁ:
phrases.english: GEMARA: Rabbi Mani bar Patish said:
What is the reason of the Rabbis?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the first case of the משנה (step 1) to find its source
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for the רבנן's view that יוצא דופן does not bring the laws of a יולדת

steps.title: The source: she must give birth from the place where she conceives
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק ״אשה כי תזריע וילדה זכר״ links the birth to the place of conception. So the יולדת laws apply only to a birth through that same place, and not to a caesarean birth.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: "When a woman conceives and gives birth to a male". This teaches that the laws apply only if she gives birth through the place where she conceives.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מני בר פטיש answers his own question with a פסוק from the section about a יולדת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק puts "תזריע" (she conceives) right next to "וילדה" (and gives birth). The רבנן read this to mean the birth must come out through the same place where the seed entered. A caesarean birth does not come out that way, so the יולדת laws do not apply.

keyTerms.meaning: She conceives (literally, she produces seed)
The place where she conceives, the normal birth canal

steps.whyThisMatters: This explains the רבנן's view in the משנה: the יולדת laws depend on how the baby is born, not only on the fact that a baby was born.

phrases.english: The verse states:
"If a woman conceives and gives birth to a male" —
phrases.notes: ויקרא 12:2

phrases.english: not unless she gives birth
through the place where she conceives.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר קְרָא אִשָּׁה כִּי תַזְרִיעַ וְיָלְדָה זָכָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 4
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק ״אשה כי תזריע וילדה זכר״ teaches that the יולדת laws apply only when she gives birth through the place where she conceives, which leaves out יוצא דופן.

steps.title: What does רבי שמעון do with the word תזריע?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי שמעון explains ״תזריע״, since he does not use it to exclude a caesarean birth.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי שמעון — what does he learn from the word ״תזריע״?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to רבי שמעון and asks what he does with the word ״תזריע״ that the רבנן just used. This short question sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every word in the תורה must teach something. Since רבי שמעון holds that a caesarean birth does count as a birth, he cannot read ״תזריע״ the way the רבנן do. So he must use it for something else.

keyTerms.meaning: Conceives (literally 'gives seed'). This is the word the רבנן used in step 5.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Shimon?
phrases.notes: He means: what does רבי שמעון do with the word ״תזריע״ from the last step?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how the other side explains the פסוק that step 5 used

steps.title: תזריע teaches about a fetus that dissolved before birth
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון uses ״תזריע״ to teach that even if the fetus came out dissolved, like the seed, the mother is still טמאה לידה.
steps.simpleTranslation: That word teaches that even if she gave birth only to something like the seed she conceived, its mother is impure because of childbirth (טמאה לידה).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי שמעון reads ״תזריע״ as teaching a new case. If the fetus dissolved and came out looking like the original fluid, the mother is still טמאה because of childbirth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן read ״תזריע״ as 'birth from the place of conception'. רבי שמעון reads it as 'even a birth that looks like the seed'. Both sides use the same word, but for different lessons.

keyTerms.meaning: Looking like the seed she conceived; a fetus that dissolved into fluid
Impure because of childbirth

phrases.english: That word comes to teach that even if she gave birth
only to something like what she conceived,
phrases.notes: The fetus melted into fluid before coming out, so it looks like the seed.

phrases.english: its mother is impure with the impurity of childbirth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי שמעון uses ״תזריע״ to make the mother טמאה even when the fetus came out dissolved

steps.title: What is רבי שמעון's source for counting a caesarean birth?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where רבי שמעון learns that a caesarean birth brings the laws of a יולדת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי שמעון — what is his reason?
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא asks for רבי שמעון's own source that a caesarean birth counts. This question sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far we only saw how רבי שמעון escapes the רבנן's proof. Now he needs a positive source of his own.

keyTerms.meaning: What is his reason / source?

phrases.english: And Rabbi Shimon, what is his reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from defending רבי שמעון to finding his positive source
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that teaches רבי שמעון's view

steps.title: The extra word תלד includes a caesarean birth
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש says that the extra word ״תלד״ comes to include a caesarean birth.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: the פסוק says ״תלד״ — to include a caesarean birth.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש gives רבי שמעון's source. The word ״תלד״ ('she gives birth') is extra, so it comes to include a caesarean birth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק already spoke about giving birth, so ״תלד״ is not needed to tell us that. An extra word is a רבוי, a sign to include more cases. For רבי שמעון, the case it adds is a caesarean birth.

keyTerms.meaning: To include; an extra word adds another case
She gives birth (ויקרא יב:ה)

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the rest of the sugya. If רבי שמעון uses ״תלד״ for a caesarean birth, we must ask what the רבנן use it for.

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
The verse says: "she gives birth" —
phrases.notes: ויקרא יב:ה

phrases.english: to include a baby born through the side (a caesarean birth).

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר קְרָא תֵּלֵד לְרַבּוֹת יוֹצֵא דּוֹפֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 8
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra word ״תלד״ includes a יוצא דופן

steps.title: What do the רבנן learn from תלד?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the רבנן do with the extra word ״תלד״.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן — what do they do with ״תלד״?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks the רבנן what they learn from the extra word ״תלד״. This short question sets up the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן do not include a caesarean birth, yet ״תלד״ is still an extra word. It must teach them something else.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis?
phrases.notes: He means: what do the רבנן learn from the extra word ״תלד״?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns step 9's source back on the רבנן

steps.title: The רבנן use תלד to include a טומטום and an אנדרוגינוס
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן need ״תלד״ to include a baby who is a טומטום or an אנדרוגינוס. Without it we would think only a definite boy or girl counts, since the פסוקים say זכר and נקבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: That word is needed to include a טומטום and an אנדרוגינוס. You might have thought that since ״זכר״ and ״נקבה״ are written, it means only a definite male and a definite female, and not a טומטום or an אנדרוגינוס. So the word teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the רבנן use ״תלד״ to include a baby whose gender is unclear. The word teaches that the birth itself is what matters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the פסוקים say 'male' and 'female', one might think only a clearly male or clearly female baby makes the mother a יולדת. ״תלד״ teaches that any birth counts, even a טומטום or an אנדרוגינוס.

keyTerms.meaning: A baby whose sexual organs are covered, so the gender is unknown
A baby with both male and female organs
You might have thought; introduces a mistaken idea
It teaches us (that the mistaken idea is wrong)

phrases.english: That word is needed by them
to include a tumtum and a hermaphrodite,
for it would enter your mind to say:
"male" and "female" are written —
phrases.notes: ויקרא יב:ב and ויקרא יב:ה

phrases.english: meaning a definite male and a definite female,
and not a tumtum or a hermaphrodite,
so it teaches us that they are included.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי מִבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לְרַבּוֹת טוּמְטוּם וְאַנְדְּרוֹגִינוֹס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 10 by giving ״תלד״ a different job for the רבנן
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: For the רבנן, ״תלד״ includes a טומטום and an אנדרוגינוס

steps.title: Where does רבי שמעון learn the טומטום case?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי שמעון includes a טומטום and an אנדרוגינוס, since he used ״תלד״ for a caesarean birth.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי שמעון — where does he learn that a טומטום and an אנדרוגינוס are included?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to רבי שמעון. It asks where he gets the טומטום and אנדרוגינוס rule, since he already used ״תלד״ for something else. This question sets up the final answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees that a טומטום and an אנדרוגינוס count as births. But רבי שמעון already 'used up' ״תלד״, so he needs another source.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Shimon?
phrases.notes: He means: where does רבי שמעון learn the rule about a טומטום and an אנדרוגינוס?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the רבנן's use of ״תלד״ into a question on רבי שמעון
steps.sheelahInformationSought: רבי שמעון's source for including a טומטום and an אנדרוגינוס

steps.title: רבי שמעון learns it from לבן and לבת
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון learns the טומטום and אנדרוגינוס rule from בר ליואי's teaching. ״לבן״ means any son and ״לבת״ means any daughter.
steps.simpleTranslation: He learns it from what בר ליואי taught: ״לבן״ — for a son in any case; ״לבת״ — for a daughter in any case.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי שמעון learns this from a different פסוק. בר ליואי taught that the words ״לבן״ and ״לבת״ include any son or daughter, even one whose gender is not definite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״לבן״ and ״לבת״ are read broadly as 'any child', so they cover a טומטום and an אנדרוגינוס too. Now each side has a source for every case: רבי שמעון uses ״תלד״ for a caesarean birth and ״לבן/לבת״ for the טומטום.

keyTerms.meaning: He derives it from
In any case; however it is
For a son... for a daughter (ויקרא יב:ו)

steps.whatToRemember: רבנן: ״תזריע״ leaves out a caesarean birth, and ״תלד״ includes a טומטום and an אנדרוגינוס. רבי שמעון: ״תזריע״ teaches about a dissolved fetus, ״תלד״ includes a caesarean birth, and ״לבן/לבת״ include a טומטום and an אנדרוגינוס.

phrases.english: He derives it from what bar Livai taught,
for bar Livai taught:
"For a son" — for a son in any case,
phrases.notes: ויקרא יב:ו

phrases.english: "For a daughter" — for a daughter in any case.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 12 with a separate source
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי שמעון learns the טומטום and אנדרוגינוס rule from ״לבן״ and ״לבת״

steps.title: What do the רבנן do with ״לבן או לבת״?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the רבנן learn from the words ״לבן״ and ״לבת״.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן? What do they do with these words?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question: רבנן did not use ״לבן או לבת״ for a טומטום and an אנדרוגינוס, so what do they learn from those words? This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון used ״לבן או לבת״ for the טומטום and אנדרוגינוס rule (step 13). רבנן learned that rule from ״תלד״ instead (step 11). So the words ״לבן או לבת״ are still unused for רבנן, and every word in the תורה must teach something.

keyTerms.meaning: For a son (part of the פסוק about the mother's קרבן)
For a daughter

phrases.english: And the Rabbis?
phrases.notes: The question is short. He means: what do the רבנן learn from ״לבן או לבת״, since they did not use it for the טומטום rule?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the same kind of question asked of רבי שמעון back onto רבנן
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the רבנן learn from the words ״לבן או לבת״

steps.title: The רבנן: a separate קרבן for every child
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן use ״לבן או לבת״ to require a קרבן for each son and each daughter.
steps.simpleTranslation: They need this to obligate her for each and every son and for each and every daughter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבנן use ״לבן או לבת״ to teach that the mother owes a קרבן for each son and each daughter she gives birth to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words ״לבן״ and ״לבת״ make each child count on its own. So a birth that comes after the earlier birth's days are over needs its own קרבן, even for twins from one pregnancy. Births close together, like ordinary twins, are still covered by one קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: He needs it (to teach something else)
To obligate, to make someone owe something
Each and every son, one by one

phrases.english: This is needed for them
to obligate her for each and every son,
and to obligate her for each and every daughter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 14
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ״לבן או לבת״ teaches that a separate קרבן is owed for each son and each daughter

steps.title: Where does רבי שמעון learn this rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where רבי שמעון learns that each child needs its own קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי שמעון? Where does he learn this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where רבי שמעון gets the rule of a separate קרבן for each child, since he already used ״לבן או לבת״ for the טומטום rule. The answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the mirror of step 14. Every rule must come from somewhere. Since רבי שמעון's ״לבן או לבת״ is already used up, he needs a different source for this rule.

keyTerms.meaning: The offering a woman brings after giving birth

phrases.english: And Rabbi Shimon?
phrases.notes: He means: where does רבי שמעון learn that each child needs its own קרבן?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks רבי שמעון for his source of the rule רבנן just derived
steps.sheelahInformationSought: רבי שמעון's source for a separate קרבן for each birth

steps.title: The ברייתא on ״זאת תורת היולדת״
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון learns it from a ברייתא on ״זאת תורת היולדת״. The ברייתא first asks whether one קרבן could cover a birth and a זיבה together.
steps.simpleTranslation: He learns it from what a reciter taught before רב ששת: ״This is the law of the woman who gives birth.″ This teaches that she brings one קרבן for many births. One might think she could bring one for a birth and for a זיבה together?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי שמעון learns the rule from a ברייתא about the word ״זאת״. The ברייתא first says one קרבן can cover many children, then asks whether one קרבן could also cover a birth and a זיבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״זאת תורת היולדת״ shows that sometimes one קרבן covers several births, for example twins. The ברייתא then looks for a limit on that rule. Its first try, birth together with זיבה, is about to be challenged in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Here: a reciter who memorized ברייתות and repeated them in the בית מדרש
This is the law of the woman who gives birth (ויקרא יב:ז)
Births, children born
A flow of blood outside the normal time, which also requires a קרבן
One might have thought

steps.confusionAlert: Here ״תנא״ does not mean a sage of the משנה. It means a person who recited ברייתות in front of רב ששת.

phrases.english: He derives it from what was taught by
a reciter before Rav Sheshet:
"This is the law of the woman who gives birth,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא יב:ז

phrases.english: teaches that she brings one offering
for many births.
One might think she may bring for a birth
and for a זיבה as one?

steps.triggerLanguage: נָפְקָא לֵיהּ מִדְּתָנֵי תַּנָּא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב שֵׁשֶׁת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 16 by quoting a ברייתא
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי שמעון learns the rule from the ברייתא's reading of ״זאת״

steps.title: That can't be the question: blood and חלב need their own קרבן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא's question. Nobody would think one קרבן covers two unrelated obligations.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a new mother who ate blood, or one who ate חלב: is one קרבן enough for her?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא interrupts the ברייתא. Why would anyone think one קרבן covers both a birth and a זיבה? A new mother who ate blood or חלב obviously needs a separate קרבן for that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Eating blood or חלב makes a person owe a חטאת for a separate sin, and nobody thinks the birth קרבן covers it. In the same way, a זיבה is a separate obligation. So the ברייתא's question about birth and זיבה makes no sense as written.

keyTerms.meaning: Blood, which is forbidden to eat
Forbidden fat of an animal
Is it enough for her?
One

phrases.english: But a woman who gave birth and ate blood,
or a woman who gave birth and ate forbidden fat,
is one offering enough for her?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the wording of the ברייתא's question in step 17
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's suggestion that one קרבן might cover a birth and a זיבה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Separate obligations, like eating blood or חלב, obviously need separate קרבנות. So the question was never a real possibility.

steps.title: The corrected ברייתא: a birth before and a birth after מלאת
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is rewritten. The real question is whether one קרבן covers a birth before and a birth after the end of the purity days, and ״זאת״ teaches that it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: one might think she could bring one קרבן for a birth before the completion and a birth after the completion together. The פסוק says ״זאת״.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the ברייתא's question. Could one קרבן cover a birth before her days of purity were done and another birth after they were done? The word ״זאת״ answers no.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both of these are births, so it is a real possibility that one קרבן covers both. ״זאת״ limits the rule: one קרבן covers several births only when they are close together, not when the second birth comes after the first one's time is finished. This is where רבי שמעון learns that separate births need separate קרבנות.

keyTerms.meaning: The completion of the mother's days of purity after a birth
The פסוק teaches us
Together, as one

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי שמעון, ״זאת״ is the source that each separate birth needs its own קרבן. For רבנן, that source is ״לבן או לבת״.

phrases.english: Rather: one might think she may bring
for a birth before the completion
and for a birth after the completion, as one?
The verse states: "This."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, יָכוֹל תָּבִיא עַל לֵידָה שֶׁלִּפְנֵי מְלֹאת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 18 by rewording the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One קרבן could cover a birth before מלאת and another birth after מלאת
steps.terutzMaskana: ״זאת״ teaches that these births need separate קרבנות

steps.title: רבנן still need ״לבן או לבת״ even with ״זאת״
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן agree that ״זאת״ is written, but say ״לבן או לבת״ is still needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן: even though ״זאת״ is written, ״לבן או לבת״ was still needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבנן don't learn the rule from ״זאת״ the way רבי שמעון does. It answers that even with ״זאת״ written, ״לבן או לבת״ was still needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since ״זאת״ already teaches about separate births, one could think ״לבן או לבת״ adds nothing for רבנן. The גמרא says that for רבנן, ״לבן או לבת״ is still needed in addition to ״זאת״. This keeps their reading of ״לבן או לבת״ in place.

keyTerms.meaning: Even though
That it is written
It was necessary

steps.whatToRemember: Both sides agree that a woman needs a separate קרבן for separate births. They only disagree on which words in the פסוק teach it.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis: even though "This" is written,
"For a son or for a daughter" was still needed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends רבנן's use of ״לבן או לבת״ now that ״זאת״ has been shown to teach a similar rule
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Even with ״זאת״, the פסוק still needed to say ״לבן או לבת״

steps.title: Why ״לבן או לבת״ is still needed: twins from one pregnancy
steps.stepSummary: ״זאת״ alone would only teach separate קרבנות for two pregnancies. ״לבן או לבת״ teaches that even twins from one pregnancy need two when they are born far apart, like רבי חייא's sons (see 27a). Twins born together still need only one.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought: two births from two pregnancies (where one was a miscarriage) need two קרבנות. But two births from one pregnancy, like יהודה וחזקיה the sons of רבי חייא, would be covered by one קרבן. So the פסוק teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the רבנן's answer from Step 20. It explains exactly what we would wrongly think if we only had ״זאת״.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״זאת״ only covers a case of two separate pregnancies, where the second birth was a miscarriage conceived later. With twins from one pregnancy, born far apart like the sons of רבי חייא, we might say one קרבן is enough. ״לבן או לבת״ teaches that each birth needs its own קרבן even then.

keyTerms.meaning: A pregnancy
A miscarriage, a baby that is not viable

steps.whatToRemember: For the רבנן, ״זאת״ covers two pregnancies, and ״לבן או לבת״ covers twins from one pregnancy born far apart. Twins born together still need only one קרבן.

phrases.english: It would enter your mind to say:
with two pregnancies (where one was a miscarriage), [two offerings are needed],
phrases.notes: Some versions have the words in round brackets and some don't.

phrases.english: but with one pregnancy,

phrases.aramaic: כְּגוֹן יְהוּדָה וְחִזְקִיָּה בְּנֵי רַבִּי חִיָּיא,
phrases.english: such as Yehuda and Chizkiyya, the sons of Rabbi Chiya,
phrases.notes: These were twins from one pregnancy, born three months apart.

phrases.english: I would say one offering is enough for her —
so it teaches us [that it is not].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the רבנן's answer from Step 20 by showing what ״לבן או לבת״ adds beyond ״זאת״.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ״לבן או לבת״ is needed for twins from a single pregnancy, which ״זאת״ alone would not cover.

steps.title: רבי שמעון agrees a יוצא דופן animal cannot become holy
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says that even רבי שמעון agrees that an animal born through the side cannot be made קדשים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן says: רבי שמעון agrees about קדשים that [an animal born through the side] does not become holy.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement begins. רבי יוחנן limits רבי שמעון's view: יוצא דופן counts as a birth for a woman, but not for making an animal holy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רבי שמעון treated a birth through the side as a real birth for a woman. רבי יוחנן says this does not carry over to animals for קדשים. Such an animal cannot become holy.

keyTerms.meaning: Agrees, concedes (on a specific point)
Animals set aside as holy for קרבנות

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: וּמוֹדֶה רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan says: And Rabbi Shimon agrees
regarding consecrated animals that it is not consecrated.
phrases.notes: "It" is an animal born through the side. Someone tries to make it holy, and it doesn't work.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: how far רבי שמעון's יוצא דופן view reaches.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even according to רבי שמעון, an animal born through the side cannot become קדשים.

steps.title: The reason: learning ״לידה״ from בכור
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון learns קדשים from בכור through the shared word ״לידה״. A בכור must be ״פטר רחם״, so the same applies to קדשים.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? He learns ״לידה״ from ״לידה″ written by בכור. Just as there it must be ״פטר רחם״, so too here it must be ״פטר רחם״.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי שמעון agrees, and answers with a גזירה שוה from בכור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ״לידה״ (birth) appears both by קדשים and by בכור. A בכור must 'open the womb' (״פטר רחם״), so a יוצא דופן never counts as a בכור. By the shared word, קדשים also require a normal birth through the womb.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
He learns (one law from another, often by a shared word)
Birth, the shared word linking the two topics
A firstborn animal
Opening the womb, meaning a natural birth

phrases.english: What is the reason?
He learns "birth" "birth" from a firstborn —
phrases.notes: ויקרא 22:27 (קדשים) and דברים 15:19 (בכור).

phrases.english: just as there it is "opening the womb,"
phrases.notes: שמות 13:15

phrases.english: so too here it is "opening the womb."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for רבי יוחנן's statement in Step 22.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why does רבי שמעון agree that a יוצא דופן animal is not holy?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה שוה of ״לידה״ from בכור, which requires ״פטר רחם״.

steps.title: Why not learn from a human birth instead?
steps.stepSummary: The word ״לידה״ also appears by a woman giving birth, where רבי שמעון counts יוצא דופן. So learn קדשים from there.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let him learn ״לידה״ from ״לידה״ written by a person: just as there יוצא דופן counts, so too here יוצא דופן should count.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the source. The same word ״לידה״ could link קדשים to a human birth, which would give the opposite result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By a woman, רבי שמעון holds that a birth through the side counts as a birth. If we connect קדשים to אדם instead of בכור, a יוצא דופן animal should become holy. So why choose בכור?

keyTerms.meaning: And let him learn (a challenge offering a different source)
A person, here a woman giving birth

phrases.english: But let him learn "birth" "birth" from a person —
phrases.notes: ויקרא 12:2

phrases.english: just as there, one born through the side [counts],
so too here, one born through the side [should count]!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the choice of בכור as the source in Step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: The גזירה שוה from בכור in Step 23
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: ״לידה״ also appears by אדם, where יוצא דופן counts. That link would give the opposite result.

steps.title: בכור is the better match: both say ״אמו״
steps.stepSummary: It is more reasonable to learn from בכור, because both בכור and קדשים use the word ״אמו״.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes more sense to learn from בכור, since it is ״אמו״ from ״אמו״.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends learning from בכור by pointing to a second shared word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוקים about קדשים and about בכור both speak of ״אמו״, 'its mother'. That extra shared word makes בכור a closer match than a human birth. So the link to בכור wins.

keyTerms.meaning: It is more reasonable
To learn (a law from another source)
Its mother, a word found in both פסוקים

phrases.english: It is more reasonable that he should learn from a firstborn,
since it is "its mother" from "its mother,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 22:27 (קדשים) and שמות 22:29 (בכור).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing a stronger textual link to one source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both בכור and אדם share ״לידה״, so either could be the source.
steps.terutzMaskana: בכור also shares ״אמו״ with קדשים, so it is the better source.

steps.title: On the contrary: ordinary from ordinary
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: learning from אדם is better, because ordinary קדשים are like ordinary human births, not like a firstborn.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary, he should learn from a person, since that is ordinary from ordinary!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer of Step 25 with a counter-argument for learning from אדם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Most קדשים are regular animals, not firstborns. A human birth in this law is also any regular birth, not only a firstborn. So אדם seems the closer match. The next step answers this by counting more shared features with בכור.

keyTerms.meaning: On the contrary
Ordinary, meaning not a firstborn

steps.confusionAlert: Here ״פשוט״ does not mean 'simple' or 'obvious'. It means an ordinary birth, the opposite of a בכור.

phrases.english: On the contrary, he should learn from a person,
since it is ordinary from ordinary!
phrases.notes: Regular (not firstborn) consecrated animals, learned from regular (not firstborn) human births.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes back against the ״אמו מאמו״ answer of Step 25.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in Step 25 that בכור is the better source
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Ordinary קדשים match ordinary human births better than a firstborn does, so אדם should be the source.

steps.title: Five features shared by בכור and קדשים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא argues that רבי שמעון should learn from בכור, because בכור and קדשים share five features: אמו, being a sacred animal, פיגול, נותר and טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he should learn it from a firstborn animal. Both share the word 'mother', both are sacred animals, and both can become פיגול, נותר and טמא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the push toward learning from אדם. It lists five things that בכור and קדשים have in common and that a human birth does not have.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 25 gave only one link, the word אמו. Now the גמרא adds four more links, all rules about sacrifices: both are sacred animals, and both can be ruined by פיגול, נותר and טומאה. None of these apply to a human baby, so בכור looks like the closer comparison.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal that is holy for the מקדש, a sacrificial animal
A sacrifice ruined by a wrong intention during its service
Sacrificial meat left over past its allowed time
Ritually impure, which makes sacrificial meat unfit

steps.confusionAlert: The word אִם here does not mean 'if'. It is a short way of saying 'mother' (אמו), the shared word from step 25.

phrases.english: Rather, he should learn it from a firstborn animal,
since they share: 'mother', a sacrificial animal,
phrases.notes: אִם is short for the word 'אמו' (its mother) that both פסוקים use.

phrases.english: פיגול, נותר, and impurity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 26 by adding more points of comparison between קדשים and בכור.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Strengthening the comparison by counting more shared features
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Learning from אדם is better, because ordinary קדשים are like ordinary births.
steps.terutzMaskana: בכור shares five features with קדשים, so it may still be the better source.

steps.title: Four features shared by human births and קדשים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back with four features that ordinary קדשים share with human births and not with בכור: ordinary, not only males, not holy from birth, and not a gift to a כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary, he should learn it from humans. Both are ordinary births, both include more than just males, both are not holy on their own, and both are not a gift to a כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא argues the other side. It lists four ways that ordinary קדשים are like a human birth and unlike a בכור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each of the four words names something special about a בכור: it is a firstborn, only males count, it is holy automatically from birth, and it is given to a כהן. Ordinary קדשים and human births have none of these. So the comparison to אדם is also strong.

keyTerms.meaning: A gift, here one of the gifts given to a כהן

phrases.english: On the contrary, he should learn it from humans,
since they share: ordinary, male, holy, as a gift!
phrases.notes: Each word names a feature of a בכור that the other two lack: firstborn, males only, holy from birth, given to a כהן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 27's five features with four features on the side of אדם.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 27 that בכור is the better source
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Ordinary קדשים differ from בכור in four basic ways, and in all four they match a human birth.

steps.title: The side with more shared features wins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא decides that בכור is the better source because its shared features are more numerous: five against four.
steps.simpleTranslation: These are more.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the debate. The five features shared with בכור outnumber the four shared with אדם, so רבי שמעון learns קדשים from בכור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When two comparisons compete, the one with more points in common is chosen. Five beats four, so קדשים follow בכור. That means an animal born through the side cannot become קדשים, which explains רבי יוחנן's statement in step 22.

keyTerms.meaning: Those, these ones
They are more numerous

steps.whatToRemember: רבי שמעון learns קדשים from בכור, not from אדם, because they share more features (5 against 4). So even רבי שמעון agrees that a יוצא דופן animal cannot be made קדשים.

phrases.english: Those are more numerous.
phrases.notes: He means the five features shared with בכור are more than the four shared with אדם.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides between the two lists in steps 27 and 28.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The comparison with more shared features wins. So קדשים are learned from בכור and must be born the normal way.

steps.title: A ברייתא of רבי יהודה that supports רבי יוחנן begins
steps.stepSummary: רב חייא בריה דרב הונא, quoting רבא, brings a ברייתא that supports רבי יוחנן. In it רבי יהודה points to three limiting words in the פסוק about the עולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חייא son of רב הונא said in the name of רבא: a ברייתא supports רבי יוחנן. רבי יהודה says: 'This is the law of the burnt offering; that is the burnt offering'. These are three words that limit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new proof for רבי יוחנן. It starts quoting a ברייתא, and the ברייתא continues in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה points out three words in the פסוק that each limit the rule: 'זאת', 'היא', and 'העולה'. So far the ברייתא has only counted them. What they leave out, and how this supports רבי יוחנן, comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: That supports, that helps prove
The law of the burnt offering
A word in the פסוק that limits or leaves out cases

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב הוּנָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרָבָא:
phrases.english: Rav Ḥiyya son of Rav Huna said in the name of Rava:
A baraita is taught that supports Rabbi Yoḥanan,
Rabbi Yehuda says:
'This is the law of the burnt offering; that is the burnt offering':
phrases.notes: ויקרא 6:2

phrases.english: these are three exclusions,
phrases.notes: The three limiting words are 'זאת', 'היא' and 'העולה'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After settling רבי שמעון's source, the גמרא brings outside support for רבי יוחנן's statement from step 22.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's statement that even רבי שמעון agrees a יוצא דופן animal cannot be made קדשים
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא of רבי יהודה reading three limiting words in ויקרא 6:2
